brief: Marketing hero image for the webex-messaging-mcp-server README: visualize the MCP server as the architectural bridge between AI assistants and Cisco Webex messaging services

generations.prompt_sent: subject: sleek isometric technical architecture illustration of a central glowing hexagonal MCP server hub node connecting a luminous AI assistant orb on the left to a constellation of Webex messaging service modules on the right (chat bubble panels, team space cards, webhook signal beacons, people directory tiles); action: streams of light data packets flowing along curved luminous pipelines from the AI orb through the central hub outward into the messaging modules; location: floating above a dark navy abstract digital plane with a subtle receding grid horizon; camera_control: three-quarter isometric aerial view, wide 16:9 framing, generous negative space in the upper third for a headline; lighting: cool teal and emerald rim light with soft cyan glows against a deep navy background, gentle volumetric haze rising from the plane; style: premium SaaS marketing hero art, clean vector-inspired 3D render, minimal and uncluttered, high polish, absolutely no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks

evals.name: alignment_score
evals.usage: ranking/filtering signal only until Phase 2 calibration (plan §5.1)

evals.feedback: Strong first-shot hero. Composition matches the architectural brief: AI assistant orb (left) feeds twin luminous pipelines - a nice accidental echo of the server's dual STDIO/HTTP transports - into a glowing central hub with a vertical light beam, fanning out right to recognizable messaging modules (chat bubble panels, people/directory tiles, webhook beacon). Deep navy grid plane, teal/emerald rim lighting, volumetric haze, and clean upper-third negative space for a headline are all present. Deviations: hub is a rounded square, not the requested hexagon (cosmetic, does not harm the marketing purpose); lower-right module cluster is slightly denser than the rest of the frame and a few cards connect via thin traces rather than full pipelines. No text, letters, logos, or watermarks anywhere. These deviations do not justify a $0.067 re-roll that would risk losing this composition (route has no seed support).
